title: Palestine, AR
description:
There are many theories about what delineates the South. As a non-Southerner writing this from a state full of snowbirds, I’m not in a position to make a black and white rule about it. But I’m allowed to notice things! Every southern state I’ve been to except for Mississippi has had at an X-Mart Adult Supercenter. These are a big deal, and are announced at least 50 miles ahead of time by billboards that alternate between counting down how many miles you have left to get there and telling you how much square footage the particular location has. In Fort Smith, Arkansas, along I-40 East, the northwesternmost X-Mart Adult Supercenter welcomes motorists to the Natural State just 5 minutes after they cross the Arkansas River (followed up by an X-Mart Adult Boutique further east in Little Rock). Like I said, I’m allowed to notice things.

East of the Supercenter and the Boutique, the Mississippi River begins to announce itself too, as I-40 enters the low-lying Arkansas Delta. The scenery opens up. Tributaries, streams, drainage ditches, irrigation canals, tangling and forking through the cultivated flatness. The fields turn the type of green that warns you that the air will be sticky next time you open the sunroof. The billboards start to lose their urgency. Eventually, nowhere in particular, you will reach the town of Palestine, Arkansas.

One of my rules for road trips is to stay at the second cheapest motel in an area. The cheapest, even by a few dollars, tends to attract the type of cigarette smoker to whom removing the batteries from a commercial smoke detector, rather than stepping right outside their hotel room to light up, is the path of least resistance.

But when you’re in a town of 700 with an auto-generated Wikipedia article, some rules must be broken. The Rest Inn Motel in Palestine, Arkansas is the only motel in Palestine, Arkansas. It costs $60 a night and there is a strong chance you will be literally the only person there, save for the Ghost of Newports Past that haunts your room. The parking spots are directly outside of the rooms, so getting your luggage in is never a hassle. The next morning, you will wake up and notice that the family who runs it is sun-roasting several pounds of fresh chilis in the parking lot on two hotel bath towels. 4.5 stars.
